key_insight: Adding preferential and differential diffusion to a tabulated-chemistry RANS model lets it capture the key thermo-diffusive behavior of lean hydrogen flames much more faithfully than unity-Lewis-number assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This improves the predictive reliability of low-cost CFD tools for hydrogen combustor design, where flame length, heat release, and stability are strongly affected by differential diffusion.
method: Extends a tabulated-chemistry model to RANS for lean premixed H2-air flames.
Solves progress-variable and mixture-fraction transport with mixture-averaged diffusion plus Soret effect.
Uses presumed-PDF turbulence–chemistry interaction and compares against DNS at Re=5500 and 11000.
evidence_signal: Against DNS for a lean H2 slot burner, the model reproduced flame length, heat-release distribution, and the equivalence-ratio/super-adiabatic temperature branches at both Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the turbulence closures used for turbulent diffusion, scalar dissipation rate, and Reynolds stresses, so implementation details can still shift results.
paper_title: Preferential and differential diffusion in RANS simulation of lean hydrogen flames with tabulated chemistry
